title: Beef Barley Soup
subtitle: Cold-night bowl that fills everyone
description: Cold-night bowl that fills everyone. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck or stew meat, cubed

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Beef Barley Soup in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Carrots, diced, Celery, diced as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Sear aromatics
steps.instruction: Brown meat in batches; remove. Sweat onion, carrot, celery in the same pot 8 minutes until edges soften. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer the pot
steps.instruction: Add broth, beef back, and pearl barley. Simmer gently 45–60 minutes until beef shreds easily and barley is tender. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Season and adjust
steps.instruction: Taste the broth and add salt and pepper until the beef and barley read clearly — the pot should taste rich, not flat. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Beef Barley Soup onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Skim and serve
steps.instruction: Skim fat if needed. Beef Barley Soup tastes better after 20 minutes off heat — hold at 180°F for late shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Beef Barley Soup on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cold-night bowl that fills everyone. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Beef Barley Soup runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
